newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian legislator accused of spreading hatred.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian legislator accused of spreading hatred.

text.p: An Indonesian legislator said on Wednesday police had summonsed him as a suspect in July riots and accused him of spreading hatred against the president and government.
"I have been accused of spreading hatred against the Indonesian President, government and public institutions," Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) legislator Aberson Sihaloho told Reuters.

Sihaloho, a member of parliament for almost 10 years, said he was the first supporter of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri to be summonsed in a government crackdown on political dissent since riots shook the capital on July 27.
The veteran legislator and founding member of the PDI said he intended to answer the summons and report to metropolitan police headquarters on Friday morning.

He was previously summonsed as a witness in the case of left-wing activist Budiman Sudjatmiko, whose underground People's Democratic Party was blamed by the government for the riots in which at least five people died and 149 were injured.
Since the riots Megawati and a number of her supporters have been questioned several times by both police and officials of the Attorney-General's department.

Sihaloho said he was summonsed over an alleged offence committed between June 17 and July 28, the period when Megawati supporters occupied PDI headquarters, holding free speech forums sometimes attended by thousands of people.
The riots started on July 27 after police raided the building and evicted the Megawati loyalists following criticism by the authorities that the forum was anti-government.
Sihaloho said he spoke only once at the forum, on July 13.
Megawati supporters occupied the headquarters after she was replaced as PDI leader by deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi at a government-backed congress in June.
Despite a military warning that Megawati and her followers do not have the right to carry out political activities, Megawati's faction set up a new headquarters in a Jakarta villa on September 9.

Faction members said on Tuesday they had received a letter from East Jakarta Mayor Sudarsono on Monday ordering the office to close within 72 hours on the grounds that it violated zoning regulations in a residential area.
In general elections scheduled for May next year, the only parties allowed to participate are the Christian-Nationalist PDI, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party and the ruling Golkar.

Electoral officials refused to accept a list of candidates from Megawati's faction of the PDI. She is currently a member of the National Assembly but was ruled out from standing in the forthcoming poll.
